title: Engineering Purpose
student: What is the purpose of an automotive engine stand, and why must its frame resist more than the engine's vertical weight?
instructor: It supports and positions an engine for service. The offset mounting head transmits gravity force and an eccentric moment to the column and base.
learningObjectives: Complete the engineering purpose task using a defensible mechanics model.

title: Components

learningObjectives: Complete the components task using a defensible mechanics model.

title: Load Path
student: Trace the gravity load path and identify where the load becomes eccentric to the column.
instructor: The engine weight enters the mounting arms and head, whose reach places the line of action a distance e from the column centerline.
learningObjectives: Complete the load path task using a defensible mechanics model.

title: Likely Column Loading
student: Predict the internal loadings in the vertical column.
instructor: The idealized column carries axial compression W and bending moment We; the assigned vertical load produces no horizontal reaction.
learningObjectives: Complete the likely column loading task using a defensible mechanics model.

title: Critical Location
student: Predict where the first-order bending stress is largest.
instructor: The constant eccentric moment is carried through the column, while the fixed base is the natural evaluation section and connection region.
learningObjectives: Complete the critical location task using a defensible mechanics model.

title: Candidate Geometry
student: Explain how increasing outside width and wall thickness changes axial and bending resistance.
instructor: Both increase area; increasing outside width especially increases second moment of area and reduces flexural stress.
learningObjectives: Complete the candidate geometry task using a defensible mechanics model.

title: Evidence Limits
student: Which assigned quantities may not be inferred from an engine-stand photograph?
instructor: Mass, eccentricity, dimensions, properties, restraint, and required safety factor are instructional assumptions, not measurements or product specifications.
learningObjectives: Complete the evidence limits task using a defensible mechanics model.

title: Idealization
student: Draw a planar idealization showing a fixed-base vertical column, the eccentric engine weight, e, H, and base reactions.
instructor: The model shows W=mg acting downward at offset e, with Rx=0, Ry=W upward, and a counterclockwise base reaction moment We.
learningObjectives: Complete the idealization task using a defensible mechanics model.

title: Assumptions
student: State assumptions required for the combined axial-plus-bending model.
instructor: Static load, prismatic square tube, linear elasticity, small deformation, fixed base, centroidal axial force plus first-order moment, and no buckling, connection, tipping, caster, dynamic, fatigue, or local-stress checks.
learningObjectives: Complete the assumptions task using a defensible mechanics model.
